newsitem.title: INDIA: India's parliament in uproar at start of session.
newsitem.headline: India's parliament in uproar at start of session.

text.p: The monsoon session of India's Parliament got off to a noisy start on Wednesday with the upper house adjourned over lawmakers' angry demands for the dismissal of two regional governments.

Witnesses said the lower house, the Lok Sabha, also erupted in angry shouting matches between government and opposition lawmakers over the situation in the eastern state of Bihar and the western state of Maharashtra.

The lower house speaker, P.A. Sangma, resisted angry demands for an adjournment and promised a statement by the Home (Interior) Minister, Indrajit Gupta, later on Wednesday on the situation in Maharashtra state.

Maharashtra has been rocked by tension between lower-caste Hindus, called Dalits, and upper caste rivals since July 11 when a state of socialist activist and Dalit leader B.R. Ambedkar was desecrated. At least 12 people died when police opened fire at rioters in Maharashtra's capital city of Bombay.
Bihar's chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav has been indicted in a corruption scandal by federal police but is resisting pressure to resign from his post.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling coalition is badly divided over its continuing association with a breakaway faction set up by Bihar's Yadav early this month, and coalition leaders are scheduled to debate the political deadlock this Friday.
